limitations: Root and delegated-child turn timing is derived from native step, tool, and conversation-return boundaries; exact provider bodies are not exposed.
Token and cost accounting are intentionally excluded.
The benchmark does not enable provider-body logging; credentials, token usage, and cost fields are never retained.
Root tool arguments are complete; delegated child arguments are the display-safe values relayed by Hermes.
Root and delegated child tool results are retained after mandatory credential and accounting-field sanitization.
Hermes exposes native durations for root and delegated child tools.
Child shell arguments are display-sanitized by Hermes before relay.
Child file-tool arguments are display-sanitized by Hermes before relay.
Child search arguments are display-sanitized by Hermes before relay.
Hermes forwards native child lifecycle, text, tool inputs, tool results, and tool durations; child model activity is represented as atomic turns without provider request or response bodies.
Hermes emits a completed compaction fact without a start boundary or duration.
The worker exposes container identity after setup; controller-owned restart, patch capture, and teardown occur outside this adapter.
Agent patch-tool activity is visible, but the controller-owned final Git snapshot is outside the worker adapter.
Native callback payloads are sanitized before persistence; accounting fields are removed by policy.
